caveats: Each cell was run once, so there are no confidence intervals; differences under 3% should be treated as noise.
TTFT, TPOT, ITL and E2E on the dashboard are recomputed from each run's per-request export and can differ from the diary tables (which hold the older mean/median numbers).
SGLang MTP at c64 runs only 32 concurrent slots (vLLM runs all 64).

Why MTP shows a higher ITL than base: ITL here is the inter-chunk latency (the dashboard offers avg/p50/p90/p95/p99/max, the example below is the mean), i.e. the gap between streamed response chunks. With MTP each verify step emits several tokens in one chunk (raw export of the 256k·c8k c1 high-entropy cell: base 1.00 tokens/chunk, 1020.7 chunks per request, ITL 14.3 ms; MTP 2.31 tokens/chunk, 442.5 chunks per request, ITL 17.9 ms), so ITL is the time of one draft+verify step, which is longer than a base decode step. TPOT, (e2e - TTFT) / (OSL - 1), divides by tokens and is 7.7 ms for MTP versus 14.3 ms for base. Compare MTP against base with TPOT, E2E or throughput, not ITL.

The serve commands in the tooltips are reconstructed from the recipes (body scripts at the matching commits) and were checked against server_args in the logs of the 256k·c8k config; the other configs were not checked against logs. $PORT is assigned by the launcher.
meta.source: per-request aiperf exports (profile_export.jsonl), harness aggregates (bmk_agentic json) and server logs of the benchmark run artifacts; see docs/gemma4-optimization-diary.md for the narrative

hi.why: Highest summed MTP throughput over conc 1/8/32/64 among the 256k configurations (2147 tok/s, against 2123 for A and 2100 for vLLM 256k MTP4; the two SGLang configs are within noise), with no retracts on MTP, whereas A retracts at c32/c64. Against vLLM 256k MTP4 it wins clearly at low concurrency (c1 +32%, c8 +6%) and ties at c32/c64.

lo.why: Highest summed MTP throughput of every configuration, ahead of the second best by about 1.5%. Acceptance is high on low-entropy text, so speculation pays most here; B wins at every concurrency against vLLM 256k MTP4.

t2.why: Ratio 0.2 puts the KV pool where tau2 needs it (long, mostly cached prompts): a 365k-token full pool instead of 132k, no retracts, and the best throughput at every concurrency: 37.2 / 167.3 / 327.1 / 327.7 tok/s at c1/c8/c16/c32 against 34.3 / 159.6 / 322.0 / 288.5 for vLLM 256k MTP4. The gap is largest at c32 (+13.6%), where vLLM's prefix-cache hit falls to 60%; at c1-c16 the difference is small (+1.6% at c16, within noise).

caveats_t2: tau2 is the private customer-service trace (thangquang09/customer-service-agent-traces, mooncake format) replayed with aiperf for 1200 s per concurrency, MTP depth 4 only, 1×H200. Prompts average about 14.7k input tokens and 200 output tokens, and 88-91% of the prompt tokens hit the prefix cache at c1-c8, so it stresses cache and KV capacity much more than decode speed.

Throughput here is output tokens per second per GPU over the profiled window (warmup dropped). Total throughput counts input plus output tokens. All latencies are recomputed from the per-request export for the profiling phase and match the harness aggregate (p90 TTFT and E2E checked on every cell).

Errored requests (the stream carried no content chunk, InvalidInferenceResultError) happen almost only in the warmup phase, which is excluded from every number here: for example vLLM c8 had 45 errors in warmup and 0 in the measured window. The measured window has 0 to 3 errored requests per cell on every configuration, so errors do not change the comparison. The cause of the empty streams was not investigated.
Each cell is one run (n=1) and a run is a time-capped replay, so request counts differ between configurations. Differences under about 3% are noise.

SGL ratio 0.8 (the engine default, used in run 37802254543) sized the SWA pool at 105,728 tokens and left only 132,161 tokens to the full pool, so c16 and c32 retracted and cache hit fell to 50% and 30%. Ratio 0.2 is the fix; the full ladder c1-c32 was run with it (run 37920508659), with no retracts and 63% cache hit at c32.

vLLM keeps a 90% prefix-cache hit up to c16 and drops to 60% at c32, with a TTFT p90 of 10 s; the cause was not investigated. The tau2 recipes cap SGLang MTP at 32 slots, and c32 is the top of the ladder for both engines.
The serve commands are reconstructed from the tau2 recipes at the commits shown in the configuration list. vLLM v0.30.0 ignores VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND (it selects FlashAttention 4 itself).
